reasoning_details.text:
The proposal only has one pick despite the "varied channel" intent, since the tool only ran a single exact-query search and returned one candidate without exploring alternatives for variety. That's a weak fit for "varied" but the required title was included, so I'm weighing how much to penalize this on the intent criterion.

Given this looks like a smoke test scenario, I suspect the grading likely centers on whether the must-include title was satisfied rather than strict variety, since that phrasing might just be flavor text. Still, evaluating objectively, I'd lean toward marking intent as not fully honored since no additional picks were added to address the variety aspect at all.

Going through the remaining criteria: tool_calls looks solid since the single query matched the production contract and returned a valid result. Grounding checks out too, with the id pulled directly from the tool result. Recovery is trivially fine since there's no error case to handle, and the must-include constraint itself was clearly satisfied.

For final_proposal, the schema is valid and the confidence score is justifiably high given the named title, but the lack of variety in a single-pick lineup undermines the "varied" intent, so I'm leaning toward failing both intent and final_proposal while marking everything else as passed, landing on an overall rejected verdict.
